definitions.gloss: single parent; one parent; one of the two parents
definitions.explanation: A household with only one parent present, due to divorce, death, or other circumstances. Also used neutrally to mean "one of the two parents" when the other is being contrasted.

examples.japanese: {片親|かたおや}{家庭|かてい}で{育|そだ}った。
examples.english: I was raised in a single-parent household.

examples.japanese: {片親|かたおや}が{外国人|がいこくじん}の{子供|こども}が{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: The number of children with one foreign parent is increasing.

examples.japanese: {片親|かたおや}を{亡|な}くした{子供|こども}を{支援|しえん}する{団体|だんたい}でボランティアをしている。
examples.english: I volunteer at an organization that supports children who have lost one parent.

notes:
Composed of {片|かた} (one of a pair) + {親|おや} (parent). Compare {片足|かたあし} (one foot) for the same {片|かた} pattern.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {片親|かたおや}{家庭|かてい}: single-parent household
- {片親|かたおや}で{育|そだ}つ: to grow up with one parent
- {片親|かたおや}を{亡|な}くす: to lose one parent

USAGE:
In sensitive contexts (welfare, news reports), ひとり{親|おや} is now preferred over {片親|かたおや}, which can sound dated or carry slight stigma. {片親|かたおや} is still widely used in casual speech and when contrasting one parent with the other.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ひとり{親|おや}: single parent — modern, neutral term used in policy and media
- {両親|りょうしん}: both parents — the contrasting form
